title: Optimal aggregation in multiclass classification
abstract: arXiv:2610.28025v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This paper studies the problem of aggregation in multiclass classification, generalizing existing results for binary classification. Given a finite dictionary of score functions F={f_1,...,f_M} and a training sample, the goal is to construct a data-driven aggregate whose risk is as close as possible to that of the best aggregate (oracle) in a prescribed subset of span(F) with respect to a given loss. In particular, we investigate model selection and convex aggregation under the 0/1 and multinomial logistic losses.   For the 0/1 loss, we show that the optimal aggregation rates remarkably do not depend on the number of classes K, and the corresponding empirical risk minimization (ERM) aggregates are rate-optimal for model selection and nearly-optimal for convex aggregation (up to an additional sqrt(ln(K)) factor). tldr: 本文将二分类的聚合理论推广到多分类，证明在0/1损失下最优聚合速率惊人地与类别数K无关，且经验风险最小化（ERM）聚合器达到最优速率。
